text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All 36 of Nigeria's state governments, in addition to local governments, have been banned from obtaining foreign loans.
- All mail handled by the Nigerian Postal Service will from 1997 be insured against theft and pilfering.
- Stockbrokers suspend trading in protest at the introduction of a new tariff.

- Managing director of Benue Cement Company has appealed to government for foreign exchange at the concesionary rate of $1=22 naira instead of market rate of $1=80 naira. He said the cost of foreign exchange was a major contributing factor to the high price of cement.
- Construction workers, worried by economic hardship and declining conditions of service, have proposed a basic minimum salary of 5,000 naira per month to their employers.
- Security officials of Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation apprehend suspects for vandalising oil distribution pipelines.
